newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says UK on course to meet EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says UK on course to meet EMU criteria.

text.p: Britain will meet the criteria demanded by the Maastricht Treaty for entering a single European currency, Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday.
"I am confident the United Kingdom will be able to achieve and sustain the convergence criteria of low inflation, low fiscal deficit and low public debt," he told parliament.
Clarke added he thought it was unlikely that European economic and monetary union (EMU) would go ahead on its scheduled start date in 1999.

"It is unlikely, though not impossible, that enough countries will be sufficiently convergent by January 1, 1999 for EMU to go ahead on that date," he said. A Conservative government would not consider joining EMU if real convergence had not been achieved, he said. "If economic and monetary union were to go ahead on any date without sufficient convergence we would not be part of it."
